correctness.rationale: A complete profile classification follows from the connected cycle-rank inequality and the forbidden induced diamond K_{2,1,1} and K_4. The hereditary one-vertex extension criterion yields exactly four non-overlapping maximal families; their counts match the stated coefficients. The combinatorial proof treats all r>=3, n_i>=1, including singleton and doubleton part boundaries. Independently coded adjacency-based enumeration checked 52 profiles/41384 subsets, plus 47 arithmetic cases; finite checks support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A canonical hereditary deletion problem receives a complete polynomial of every minimal solution on all complete multipartite graphs with at least three parts. The balanced vertex-transitive case exhibits a growing forbidden cardinality interval while the uniformly chosen maximal configuration almost surely has constant size four and the optimum grows linearly. This precise typical-vs-extremal separation is relevant to understanding greedy maximal deletion complements and is not a routine scalar optimization restatement.
